cards.explanation: The answer is True. The writer says, "My soul cleaves to the dust; revive me according to Your word." (Psalm 119:25) He doesn't pretend he's doing fine down there. He just says where he is and asks the LORD for help, and that's a good way to pray.

The answer is to be taught God's statutes. The writer says, "I recounted my ways, and You answered me; teach me Your statutes." (Psalm 119:26) God answers him, and his very next ask is to learn more. I think that's a man who wants to keep listening.

The answer is to meditate on God's wonders. The writer says, "Make clear to me the way of Your precepts; then I will meditate on Your wonders." (Psalm 119:27) First the way gets clear, then he meditates on God's wonders. Understanding leads him to wonder.

The answer is strengthen. The writer says, "My soul melts with sorrow; strengthen me according to Your word." (Psalm 119:28) He's melting, and he asks to be strengthened. Strength is a good thing to ask for when you feel like a puddle.

The answer is the way of truth. The writer says, "I have chosen the way of truth; I have set Your ordinances before me." (Psalm 119:30) Just before that, he asked to be removed from the path of deceit. Truth is the road he picked.
The answer is False. The writer says, "I have set Your ordinances before me." (Psalm 119:30) Before him, not behind him. He sets God's ordinances in front of him.

The answer is True. The writer says, "I cling to Your testimonies, O LORD; let me not be put to shame." (Psalm 119:31) He holds on tight and asks the LORD not to let him be put to shame. It's a prayer with a good grip behind it.

The answer is because God will enlarge his heart. The writer says, "I run in the path of Your commandments, for You will enlarge my heart." (Psalm 119:32) The reason is what God will do for him. He runs because God will enlarge his heart.

The answer is False. The writer says, "Teach me, O LORD, the way of Your statutes, and I will keep them to the end." (Psalm 119:33) He doesn't stop once he's learned them. He promises to keep them to the end.

The answer is understanding. The writer says, "Give me understanding that I may obey Your law, and follow it with all my heart." (Psalm 119:34) He asks for understanding first, so he can obey with his whole heart. Not half a heart, all of it.

The answer is True. The writer says, "Direct me in the path of Your commandments, for there I find delight." (Psalm 119:35) He finds delight on that path. He doesn't say he's gritting his teeth, he says delight.

The answer is covetous gain. The writer says, "Turn my heart to Your testimonies and not to covetous gain." (Psalm 119:36) He wants his heart turned toward God's testimonies and away from covetous gain. He asks God to do the turning.

The answer is reverence. The writer says, "Establish Your word to Your servant, to produce reverence for You." (Psalm 119:38) He asks God to establish His word to him. Reverence for God is what he wants that word to produce.

The answer is that God's judgments are good. The writer says, "Turn away the disgrace I dread, for Your judgments are good." (Psalm 119:39) His reason is about God, not about himself. He asks because God's judgments are good.

The answer is to answer the one who taunts him. The writer says, "Then I can answer him who taunts, for I trust in Your word." (Psalm 119:42) With God's loving devotion and salvation in place, he can answer the one who taunts him. His footing comes from trusting God's word.
The answer is False. The writer says, "Then I can answer him who taunts, for I trust in Your word." (Psalm 119:42) The trust he names is in God's word. His own strength isn't mentioned.

The answer is in freedom. The writer says, "And I will walk in freedom, for I have sought Your precepts." (Psalm 119:45) He ties his freedom to seeking God's precepts. I think that's a surprise to a lot of people.

The answer is True. The writer says, "I will speak of Your testimonies before kings, and I will not be ashamed." (Psalm 119:46) He says he will speak before kings, and he says he will not be ashamed. That's a bold line.

The answer is loves. The writer says, "I delight in Your commandments because I love them." (Psalm 119:47) His delight comes from love. He says it again in the next verse, where he calls them commandments "…which I love…" (Psalm 119:48)
